# ethereum-optimism/specs Daily Update (May 4, 2026)
## OVERVIEW 
Today's activity focused on closing several long-standing issues related to interop stress testing, supernode functionality, and Kona prestate builds, alongside a new pull request for post-execution transaction and SDM specs.

## KEY TECHNICAL DEVELOPMENTS

- **Interop Stress Testing and Performance Analysis:** Extensive stress testing on the interop devnet confirmed linear cost scaling for message validation, with a fix for Kona EIP-2935 proof decoding. This analysis provides confidence in the system's performance within the expiry window.
- **Supernode and Acceptance Test Enhancements:** Several issues related to `op-supernode` were closed, including the migration of "after head" tests to the acceptance test framework and a decision to not implement unsafe super roots. This improves testing robustness and clarifies supernode behavior.
- **Kona Prestate Build Optimization:** The process for building Kona prestates was optimized to no longer require Docker, improving local development velocity.

## NEWLY OPENED PULL REQUESTS
- A new pull request, [#908](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/pull/908), was opened to introduce specifications for Post-Execution transactions and the Superchain Data Model (SDM).

## CLOSED ISSUES

- **Interop Chain Creation and Supernode Functionality:** Issues related to creating new chains post-interop and fetching super roots from `op-supernode` for unsafe data were closed. The decision was made to generate L2 genesis with interop enabled in a dependency set of 1, and to work around super root fetching in tests rather than modifying `op-supernode` behavior ([#15884](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/issues/15884), [#19059](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/issues/19059)).
- **Kona Prestate and Acceptance Test Improvements:** The issue concerning slow Kona prestate builds was closed as a faster, non-Docker method is now available. Additionally, all missed "after head" tests were successfully migrated to `op-supernode` and `op-acceptance-test`, leading to a bug fix in `op-supernode` ([#19057](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/issues/19057), [#20370](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/issues/20370)).
- **Duplicate Issue Resolution:** A duplicate issue regarding `op-challenger` using the incorrect prestate URL for `SuperPermissionedGameType` was identified and closed ([#20500](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/issues/20500)).

## NEW ISSUES
No new issues were opened today.

## ACTIVE ISSUES

- **Interop: Stress test expiry window** ([#15285](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/issues/15285)): The latest comments confirm that extensive stress testing on the `interop-jnt-v1` devnet, including Kona interop running in Cannon/MIPS against old initiating messages, has been successful. A Kona EIP-2935 proof decoding issue was identified and fixed. The testing showed linear cost scaling with message count, suggesting that increasing the message age to the full 7-day expiry window is unlikely to cause completion issues. The analysis is considered sufficient to be confident about performance, and the issue is nearing closure pending the merged RLP decoding fix.
- **[L2CM] Milestone: Acceptance testing on Betanet** ([#20089](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/issues/20089)): This issue was identified as a duplicate of [#18839](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/issues/18839).
- **Runbook: Update super root chain from permissioned to permissionless with OPCMv2** ([#20473](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/issues/20473)): It was suggested to defer this documentation update until after interop has shipped, as it's only relevant when a chain has upgraded to SuperDisputeGame (U20+) and then transitions from permissioned to permissionless. The interop release is a precondition for this, so it should not block the current release.
